main_text.p: persecutio (vt inquit Eutropius) omnibus aliis diuturnior atque immanior. Nam per decem annos incendiis Ecclesiarum, proscriptionibus innocentium, caedibus Martyrum, incessabiliter acta est: de huius etiam persecutionis acerbitate, Christianorum-que in perferendis tormentis alacritate, Seuerus Sulpitius haec tradit; [ Omnis fere Martyrum cruore orbis infectus est;quippe certatim gloriosis in certamina ruebatur, multoque avidius tum Martyria gloriosa mortibus quaerebantur, quàm nunc Episcopatus prauis ambitionibus appetuntur: Nullis unquam magis bellis mundus exhaustus est, neque maiori unquàm Triumpho vicimus; quàm cum decem annorum stragibus vinci non potuimus.

Et certè, videtur Diabolus sui quodammodo pæsagus[?] ruituri domini, nullum non movisse lapidem, nihil reliquisse intentatum; sed omnes pariter effudisse vires ad lumen Evangelii non obscurandum modò, sed penitus extin-guendum

page.notes: Text is printed in two-column-free single column; the printed quotation marks („) at the line ends of the first paragraph are reproduced as printed. Spelling of u/v and i/j changed per rule (e.g. "unquam", "avidius", "Evangelii", "aliis", "movisse"). "pæsagus" is doubtful: the letters read as pæsagus, possibly præsagus[?]. Right of the text, near the top of the margin, there is a small mark (apostrophe-like) that appears to be a stain or show-through, not a note, so it is not transcribed. The figure "1" to the left of the last line ("guendum") is not a catchword or signature; it is left out as uncertain. The bracket "[" before "Omnis" is printed as shown. The head "Non anni domuère decem." is an italic side-title above the second paragraph, set off by a dash ornament; it is given as level 2.
